casos.pregunta: ¿Por qué Syndrome’s Remote puede dispararse en el turno rival y Buzz’s Arm no puede jugarse normalmente cuando Buzz es desterrado en ese turno?
casos.resumen_respuestas: La respuesta distingue el disparo de Syndrome’s Remote, que se pone en la bolsa, del permiso estático de coste alternativo de Buzz’s Arm, que sigue necesitando una ocasión legal para jugar el objeto.

preguntas.texto:
Hey Alain, I know this is a very old post but I'm looking to learn more about this ruling. 

What is the difference with Syndrome's Remote being able to trigger and banish this item and discarding to draw.

As compared to Buzz's Arm not being able to be played when Buzz Lightyear is banished on your opponent's turn?

Saw a video of Googly Glimmers recently on the Buzz's Arm so I would like to learn more about it. Because it feels similar to me

respuestas.autor_original: Jacob Smith [LRH], Etiqueta de servidor: LRHLRHLore Guide
respuestas.texto:
There are two different types of abilities at play here. 

LEARN FROM THEIR LOSSES is a triggered ability. When its condition is met ("whenever a robot character is banished") its effect is put into the bag. ("You may banish this item to draw two cards.") When the bag is next resolved, you take the effect out and resolve it. 

MISSING PIECE is a static ability that is always applying. If a Buzz was banished, it gives an alternate method for playing Buzz's Arm. It doesn't ever resolve or get played, it just is always checking and giving you that option when it's appropriate. 
In order to take advantage of that alternate cost, you still need to be able to play the item, which you usually only have the ability to do during your own main phase. (editado)lunes, 15 de junio de 2026, 14:

contexto.texto: @Jacob SmithSyndrome's Remote
@Jacob SmithBuzz's Arm
Replying so you have a ping ^
Thank you Jacob! Good to learn something new.

validacion.comprobacion: El disparo de Syndrome's Remote entra en la bolsa aunque ocurra en el turno rival. Buzz's Arm solo ofrece un coste alternativo para jugar un objeto; hace falta una ventana legal para jugarlo.

Agree with @dihensoeur, I wouldn't allow it as it's no longer their turn and they want to change the board state by more than one action.

In a casual game, yeah you probably would allow it.

Something I'm trying to drum into my locals is calling lore guides when someone wants to do a take back. As players are allowing take backs with multiple steps to happen which is no bueno.

There doesn't seem to be a restriction on takebacks just because the action you want to take back is passing you turn. The specific example of an ineligible takeback is waiting until your opponent has already taken an action.
A takeback is performed based on the action to takeback, not on the other potential actions that the player wants/could do.

if someone passes the turn... and then instantly is like, actually can we do a takeback

respuestas.texto:
The idea is not "Take back only one action to get the opportunity to do only one action", as long as you asked to take back one action and it was allowed you can continue doing any number of legal game actions.
If however it was the reversed, like the player moved the character to a location, passed the turn and required a take back to finally not move it, the action of passing the turn would resonnably be allowed to take back but not the action to move the character.

Yep from my understanding take back has nothing to do with what they want to do after the take back. Player can say hey can you pause so I can call a judge. If they are still in the ready phase then asking for a take back of a end turn (as long as nothing happened on the end of turn phase) would most likely be granted.

Cinderella draws a card, so perhaps not the best example of just purely passing and resolving an ability.

Maybe something like the Judy Hopps that readies a character.

But in all but the most unusual of circumstances, I’d probably consider that a batched action - people will usually pass and resolve in the same “move”. Of course, having multiple abilities to resolve would be less likely to be allowed a take back, but it all depends on how the actions were taken.

preguntas.texto:
Seeking clarification on the new rule changes for damage.

If my character receives [ACT OF KINDESS] from my [Rapunzel - Ready for Adventure], what happens when opponent challenges it with a character with 0 strength?

Since the opposing character would literally under new terms “deal 0 damage”, and then “dealt 0 damage” to my character. Would the replacement effect of [ACT OF KINDNESS] be consumed? Since it just reads “the next time they would be dealt damage”. I would assume “dealt 0 damage” still causes it to be consumed since 0 is a valid damage.

Hmm, still kinda weird, what if the opposing character had 1 strength, but is applied an effect of -1 strength (lets say by Rhino - One-Sixteenth Wolf). 

Since the damage is now modified, 1.9.5 will apply. Does this mean the eventual “dealt 0 damage” during Damage Calculation step will consume Rapunzel’s shield?

respuestas.texto:
1.9.5. If a character or effect would deal damage and that damage is reduced to 0 when modifiers are applied, the character or effect is still considered to “deal” damage.

If the character has a strength of 0 or less, then the character wouldn't deal damage in the first place, so 1.9.5 doesn't apply.

I would have thought that 1.9.5 was for things like resist, where there was damage but it was negated. The rhino example above would (in my mind) deal no damage because they had 0 strength and therefore there was no damage in the first place. I'm likely wrong though!

Even with the addition of 1.9.5, 5.3.6.2 still applies:

5.3.6.2. Strength  – Primarily, how much damage this character deals in a challenge, though card effects can also reference this value. If a character would deal damage equal to its  and it has 0 or less , it deals no damage.

contexto.texto:
In my mind, I’m just thinking, since now everything is “Deal” -> “Dealt” -> “Take”.

And Rapunzel did not specifically state “the next time they would be dealt more than 1 damage”…in this case would a “dealt 0 damage” event consume the shield since “dealt 0 damage” is, to me, still considered “the next time they would be dealt damage”.

Under 4.6.6.1 “First, calculate the total amount of damage dealt to each character in the challenge. If a character’s strength is negative, it counts as 0 strength for the purpose of determining how much damage is dealt during the challenge.”

It does not explicitly state that if the character strength is 0, the “dealt 0 damage” event does not occur at all in 4.6.6.2.
Ah great, ty. I was zoomed in on the challenge clauses and missed this. So indeed there is a clause which is 5.3.6.2 to explicitly state that 0 strength means deal no damage.
Guess there will be no 0 damage shenanigans to remove Rapunzel’s shield.

validacion.comprobacion: Fuerza 0 significa que el personaje no inflige daño durante el desafío; no hay daño que consumiría Act of Kindness. Esto es distinto de infligir daño y que Resist lo reduzca después.

respuestas.autor_original: Danxor [LRH], Etiqueta de servidor: LRHLRHCommunity Collaborator
respuestas.texto: I would assume yes
There is nothing special about it other thn starting in play from outside the game.
Yeah, once the game starts it’s just in play and behaves like any other item.

contexto.texto: Thanks! That's what we had assumed as well.

validacion.comprobacion: Una vez que Robin's Bow está en juego es un objeto normal y You're Welcome puede barajarlo si es un objetivo legal. Lo no definido por Coconut es cómo una carta de la «collection» entra en juego y pasa a ser una carta del juego.
